title: CAR-T cell therapy for solid tumors
bottleneck: CAR-T cells have produced durable remissions in blood cancers but largely fail against solid tumors, which present a hostile immunosuppressive microenvironment, dense physical barriers, antigen heterogeneity that enables escape, and on-target off-tumor toxicity risks.
why_it_blocks: Solid tumors cause the vast majority of cancer deaths; until engineered cell therapies work in them, CAR-T's transformative impact stays confined to hematologic malignancies.
current_state: Next-generation approaches, including armored CARs secreting cytokines, TCR-engineered cells, tumor-infiltrating lymphocyte therapies, and combinations that remodel the microenvironment, are in clinical trials with early signals. Making shielded, cold solid tumors responsive remains unsolved. Key advances include engineering T cells to resist exhaustion, targeting multiple antigens at once, and pairing cell therapy with drugs that dismantle the suppressive stroma. Early-phase trials are testing these combinations, but durable responses in solid tumors remain rare.
